lab_title: AR Lab: Structural Anatomy of the Heart & Dual-Loop Blood Flow
top_level_objectives: Identify the four heart chambers and their relative positions (right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, left ventricle).
Identify the four major valves and the vessels that enter and leave the heart (SVC/IVC, pulmonary arteries/veins, aorta).
Trace the path of deoxygenated and oxygenated blood through right- and left-sided flow loops.
Explain why the left ventricle has thicker myocardium than the right ventricle using circulation workload and connect it to dual-loop flow.
Describe how cardiac valves prevent backflow during the cardiac cycle using the sequence of chamber-to-vessel connections.

scenes.brief_purpose: Establish spatial orientation of the heart and orient students to the AR model for correct chamber identification.
key_visuals: 3D heart model centered in AR space with anatomical orientation cues (anterior view markers).
Color-coded placeholder regions indicating expected chamber locations (right vs left).
On-screen labels for major external landmarks (e.g., septum boundary cue).
student_actions: Rotate/scale the model to match an anatomical view (anterior-to-posterior and right/left orientation).
Point out where the atria are relative to the ventricles and confirm the approximate right-side vs left-side of the model using the AR labels.

scenes.brief_purpose: Build mastery of chamber identification by having students isolate and name the four chambers.
key_visuals: AR callouts that highlight right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, left ventricle one at a time.
Subtle depth cues showing atria superior to ventricles.
Optional myocardium thickness overlay ready to compare later (right vs left region shading).
student_actions: Select each chamber label in sequence (RA → RV → LA → LV).
Confirm relationships: atria receive blood; ventricles pump blood—by matching each chamber to its functional cue on the screen.

scenes.brief_purpose: Connect chamber boundaries to the valves and reason how they direct flow and prevent reverse flow.
key_visuals: Valve callouts that appear at chamber-to-chamber or chamber-to-vessel transitions: tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral/bicuspid, aortic.
Flow-direction arrows between chambers and vessels.
Valve timing prompt (static overview) indicating “open/closed” states without full cycle animation details.
student_actions: Identify each valve by selecting its label when prompted.
Drag/trace a suggested flow path that starts in an atrium and ends in the next chamber/vessel, noting which valve would block backflow if reversed.

scenes.scene_name: Major Vessels Entering & Leaving the Heart
scenes.brief_purpose: Map the systemic and pulmonary inflow/outflow vessels around the heart to support later tracing of dual-loop circulation.
key_visuals: Highlighted vessel network around the heart: SVC/IVC entering the right atrium; pulmonary arteries leaving; pulmonary veins entering the left atrium; aorta leaving the left ventricle.
Distinct color coding for “systemic” (body loop) vs “pulmonary” (lung loop) vessels.
Simple directional arrows indicating inflow vs outflow relative to the heart.
student_actions: Place each vessel label correctly (SVC, IVC, pulmonary arteries, pulmonary veins, aorta) based on visual association to the heart’s appropriate chambers.
Verify inflow/outflow logic by predicting which vessels are associated with oxygen-poor vs oxygen-rich blood (using the provided color legend).

scenes.brief_purpose: Have students actively trace the complete circulation route, reinforcing the sequence and transitions at each valve.
key_visuals: Stepwise animated tracing that connects: RA → tricuspid → RV → pulmonary valve → pulmonary arteries → lungs → pulmonary veins → LA → mitral → LV → aortic valve → aorta.
Waypoints at each chamber and valve with brief labels.
Oxygen status color shift after the lungs waypoint.
student_actions: Use the trace tool to follow the prompted path from deoxygenated blood starting at the right atrium.
Answer a quick check: identify the valves crossed at each transition (e.g., which valve connects RA to RV).

scenes.brief_purpose: Explain the functional morphology: why the left ventricle has thicker myocardium based on systemic circulation workload.
key_visuals: Thickness comparison overlay between right and left ventricles (e.g., right thinner, left thicker) with a “pressure/workload” metaphor.
A simplified system-versus-pulmonary loop scale cue (body loop larger distance).
Prompted highlight of the left ventricle pumping to the aorta and systemic vessels.
student_actions: State the relationship: thicker LV myocardium corresponds to higher force needed to pump through the systemic loop.
Correlate chamber-to-vessel sequence with workload by pointing to where the left ventricle’s output enters the aorta.
